root_idea.summary: The root centers on something entering, disappearing into, or being concealed within a hollow or recess.
root_idea.development: From this spatial notion, the lexicon develops usages for descent and settling, setting or eclipse, concealment, and various specialized cavity-related applications.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed as the normalized Form I perfect citation form وَقَبَ.

senses.definition: To come in upon and settle over, or spread through, as night or darkness.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic construction with غَاسِقٍ, the subject is night or darkness; the expression describes its onset and enveloping presence, rather than the general spatial sense of entering a cavity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A hollow, cavity, socket, or hole: especially a small hollow in rock or mountain where water collects; a body socket or cavity; a pit above a horse’s eye; or a hole receiving a pulley axle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The particular cavity may be geological, anatomical, equine, or mechanical.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To enter, including to enter into a hollow or cavity.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intransitive use; the destination may be expressed as a وَقْبٌ or understood from context.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To set, of the sun; to enter its place of setting.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional usage describing the sun’s disappearance below the horizon.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To enter an eclipse, of the moon; to pass into the cone-shaped shadow of the earth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used specifically of the moon during an eclipse.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For the eyes to become sunken or depressed in the head.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a person’s eyes.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make a sound with the prepuce through movement of the penis, of a horse.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized animal and anatomical usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become absent, hidden, or concealed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The subject may be a person or a thing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To come, approach, or advance.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A movement-related intransitive use distinct from becoming hidden or entering a cavity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a palm tree to become rotten in the fruit-bearing stalks of its racemes.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a palm tree and its fruit-bearing stalks.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To hunger or suffer hunger.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a person or people.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To put a thing into a hollow or cavity.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The object is caused to enter a وَقْبَة or وَقْب.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A stupid, foolish, or dull-witted person.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Recorded as an epithet, especially of a man; the plural is أَوْقَابٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A despised, contemptible, low, base, or ignoble man.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A derogatory personal epithet.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An enlarged stomach sac in the belly of a sheep, goat, or similar animal, resembling the specified stomach organ.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical anatomical term restricted in the lexical evidence to animals of the شَاء class.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A large aperture or hole in a wall in which there is shade; also a cavity or hollow in a vessel, stone, or food preparation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes cavities such as the hollow of a vessel for ointment or the cavity of a dish of tharīd.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Fond of, or inclined toward, the company of stupid or foolish people.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival description derived from أَوْقَابٌ in its sense ‘foolish persons’.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The meaner sort of utensils and household or tent furniture.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A plural lexical item used for the ordinary equipment of a house or tent.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Highly penetrating sexually, specifically of a penis.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized anatomical adjective.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A well whose water sinks into the earth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the expression رَكِيَّةٌ وَقْبَاءُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The shell known as a cowry.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A lexical name for the shell, synonymous with وَدَعَةٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A man who drinks much water or much of the beverage called نَبِيذٌ.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The defining feature is habitual or excessive drinking.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A stupid or foolish woman; also, a woman said to give birth to stupid or foolish children.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A feminine personal epithet with the two reported applications.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A woman possessing a vulva.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized anatomical usage of the epithet.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A reproachful appellation for a group, referring disparagingly to their mother.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A fixed or conventional expression rather than a general kinship term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A journeying continued for a full day and night together.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional expression describing uninterrupted travel.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Covered by the broader cavity and socket sense.
Covered by the broader cavity and socket sense.
Covered by the broader cavity and hole sense.
Proverbial illustration and alternate-form note; it adds no independent branch for this root.
Covered by the broader cavity and hollow sense.

cautions: The foolish-person sense of وَقْبٌ is recorded in the lexical evidence, but the root analysis treats it as an ibdāl from وَغْبٌ; it should not be conflated with the cavity and entry semantic center.
The Quranic form has one occurrence and is represented specifically in its night-or-darkness construction; the contextual gloss “it spreads” does not create an additional independent sense.
